SMART Studio

SMART Studio is the tool for viewing and authoring SMART Recommendations. An expert models a Recommendation on a canvas of subjects, processes, and mappings, and the model itself is the published artifact: versioned, validated, and citable back to the source document.

Purpose

A SMART Recommendation begins as an expert reading of a published OIML Recommendation. The Studio is where that reading becomes a model: the requirements, tests, and forms are drawn as a structured graph, each element carrying its provenance. The Studio removes the gap between the document and the machine-readable form, because the model the expert draws is the model the program publishes.

What the Studio provides

  • The model canvas. A Recommendation is authored as a graph: subjects, attributes, processes, and mappings, drawn and connected directly.
  • Inspectors. Every node carries its properties, constraints, and provenance in a structured inspector, validated as it is edited.
  • The document map. Each model element cites its clause in the source publication, so the model reads against the document line by line.
  • Validation. The package is checked as it is built: schema, semantics, and the drift guards that keep a published model honest.

Lineage

The Studio descends from the MMEL editor built for the first SMART-document pilots, rebuilt on the Primmel language and the current platform. The editing model is unchanged: graphical construction of the subject, its aspects, its processes, and the mappings between reference and implementation models. The current Studio adds validation, packaging, and the direct hand off to the OIML-CS SMART platform.

Where the Studio sits

The Studio is the authoring half of the toolchain. The OIML-CS SMART platform is the running half: what an expert authors in the Studio, the platform renders, tests, and certifies. The Studio is developed as part of the Primmel platform, and the OIML SMART program builds its Recommendation authoring practice on it.
